notes: Array-to-pointer conversion and array-parameter adjustment are established C rules and remain present in C17 and C23. These examples use C99 loop declarations and size_t formatting. Newer standards do not attach array-length metadata to an ordinary pointer.

examQuestions.question: Explain two differences between an array object and a pointer variable, using sizeof and assignment.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An array owns its elements and sizeof gives their total storage in the declaring scope. A pointer owns an address and sizeof gives pointer storage. A pointer variable can be redirected; an array cannot be assigned another array or incremented. Most uses of the array expression produce a first-element pointer without changing the array object.

examQuestions.question: Read four ints from -100 to 100. Print Reverse four: then the reversed array. Swap through left and right pointers.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int a[4];
    puts("Reverse four:");
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        if (scanf("%d", &a[i]) != 1 || a[i] < -100 || a[i] > 100) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    int *left = a;
    int *right = a + 3;
    while (left < right) {
        int temp = *left;
        *left++ = *right;
        *right-- = temp;
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        printf("%s%d", i == 0 ? "" : " ", a[i]);
    }
    putchar('\n');
    return 0;
}

The fixed count guarantees valid first and last positions.
